newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's return won't help Russia, Zyuganov says.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's return won't help Russia, Zyuganov says.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's return to the Kremlin will not help solve any of the nation's problems, Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov said on Monday.
"Yeltsin is in no condition to resolve even a single issue facing Russia today," Zyuganov told a press conference. "Even when he was very healthy, he did not address a single issue facing Russia.

Yeltsin, who beat Zyuganov in the presidential election earlier this year, resumed work at the Kremlin on Monday after undergoing a quintuple heart bypass operation in November. In remarks to the nation on Friday, Yeltsin promised to work vigorously upon his return.
Zyuganov, who leads the largest faction in the Russian parliament, said that a man recovering from major surgery does not have the stamina to lead a country beset with problems.
"The leader today needs to work 15 hours a day, every day without days off," he said. "He should always be in the captain's station to make decisive decisions."
Zyuganov said his party would both confront the government with organised protests and work together in constructive dialogue. He hailed recent regional election results as "a complete success."

Of 15 gubernatorial races on Sunday, candidates from the communist-led Union of National and Patriotic Forces won in four regions and are strong contenders in two others where run-offs are scheduled, Russian news agencies reported.

Zyuganov is hoping that support from regions across Russia will make it easier for him to oppose the policies of the president, who under the Russian constitution has a stronger hand than the legislature.
